title: Signs of Crawl Space Contamination in Your Home
h1: What Are the Signs of Crawl Space Contamination?
description: Musty smells, droppings, damp soil, sagging insulation and pest activity are common signs of crawl space contamination. Learn what to look for and what to do.
quick_answer: The most common signs of crawl space contamination are musty or ammonia-like smells inside the house, rodent droppings or nests, damp soil or standing water, mold on joists or subfloor, insulation that's wet or hanging down, and torn ductwork. If the smell gets stronger when the heat or AC runs, the crawl space may be feeding the air you breathe.
body:
Many older homes in San Diego County and Orange County sit on raised foundations with a crawl space underneath. It's out of sight, so problems there can go unnoticed for years. But air from a crawl space moves up into the house through gaps in the floor, and if ducts run down there, the HVAC system can pull that air straight into your rooms.

What smells point to a crawl space problem?

Your nose is often the first warning. Pay attention to:

  • Musty or earthy odors that are worse in rooms near floor vents or along the floor
  • An ammonia or urine smell, which usually means rodents or other animals
  • A sour or rotten smell, which can mean a dead animal or a sewer leak
  • Smells that get stronger when the heat or AC turns on, a sign that air is being pulled from the crawl space into the duct system

What can I see from the crawl space opening?

You don't need to crawl all the way under the house to spot many problems. With a flashlight at the access hatch or vent, look for:

  1. Droppings, nests, chewed insulation or tracks in the dirt
  2. Standing water, wet soil or water stains on the foundation
  3. White, black or green growth on wood joists and the subfloor
  4. Insulation that's sagging, falling down or dark with moisture
  5. Torn, crushed or disconnected ducts
  6. Damaged vent screens or gaps where animals could get in
  7. Piles of debris, old construction scrap or trash

Wear a mask and gloves, and don't go in if you see a lot of droppings or standing water. Disturbing droppings can release dust that carries disease.

What signs show up inside the house?

Crawl space problems often show up upstairs in the living space. Watch for floors that feel damp or cold, wood floors that cup or warp, more dust than usual, insects coming up through gaps, scratching noises under the floor at night, and allergy symptoms that ease when you leave the house.

What causes crawl space contamination?

Moisture and pests cause most of it. Rain runoff that drains toward the house can soak the soil under it. Leaking plumbing adds water from above. Coastal humidity can lead to condensation on cool surfaces. Once things stay damp, mold follows.

Rodents get in through broken vent screens, gaps around pipes and openings in the foundation. Once inside, they nest in insulation and leave droppings and urine behind. In homes with ducts under the floor, they can also tear into the ductwork.

How is a contaminated crawl space cleaned up?

A thorough cleanup usually goes in this order:

  1. Find and fix the source, such as a plumbing leak, drainage issue or entry point.
  2. Remove contaminated insulation, droppings, nests and debris with protective gear.
  3. Sanitize the affected surfaces.
  4. Seal entry points and repair vent screens.
  5. Repair or replace damaged ductwork.
  6. Install new insulation and, where it fits the home, a vapor barrier over the soil.

Our attic and crawl space cleaning service handles removal, sanitizing, sealing and new insulation. If the ducts under the house are damaged or dirty, our air duct team can repair, seal or clean them as part of the same project.

Can I clean the crawl space myself?

Picking up a little loose debris is fine. Rodent waste, mold and wet insulation are a different story. They need protective equipment and careful handling so you don't spread contamination into the house. If you find any of those, it's safer to have it done professionally.

If you do go under the house to look, tell someone before you go in, bring a good light and watch for nails, broken glass and old wiring. Many crawl spaces are tight and dark, and it is easy to bump into ductwork or plumbing. If the space is too tight to move safely, a professional inspection with a camera and photos is the better route.
faqs: Can a crawl space affect indoor air quality?
Yes. Air moves up from the crawl space into the house through gaps in the floor. If ducts run under the house and have leaks, the HVAC system can pull crawl space air directly into your rooms.
Do most San Diego homes have crawl spaces?
Many newer tract homes are built on concrete slabs with no crawl space. Older homes and some hillside homes often have raised foundations with a crawl space underneath.
Is it dangerous to clean up rodent droppings?

It can be. Dry droppings and urine can carry disease, and sweeping or vacuuming them raises dust. Health agencies advise wetting them with disinfectant and wearing protection. Large cleanups are best left to professionals.
How do I keep rodents out of my crawl space?
Keep vent screens intact, seal gaps around pipes and wires, trim plants away from the foundation and don't leave pet food or fallen fruit nearby.
